It involves the use of high doses of the drug methotrexate, often in combination with other chemotherapies and the immunotherapy drug rituximab. It is used to block the body's use of folate, a form of vitamin B, which prevents lymphoma cells from multiplying and spreading as quickly.

nodes.label: Intrauterine Device (IUD)
nodes.description: A type of barrier method and hormonal birth control device that can be used to prevent pregnancy during cancer treatment, inserted into the uterus. A type of long-acting reversible contraceptive method mentioned as an option for birth control, along with barrier methods. A type of hormonal birth control method that may be recommended for use during cancer treatment as a barrier method to prevent pregnancy. A type of hormonal birth control method, also known as an intrauterine device, that can be used as a birth control option during cancer treatment. A type of barrier method and hormonal birth control option for individuals undergoing cancer treatment to prevent pregnancy. A type of hormonal birth control method that may be recommended or not recommended for preventing pregnancy during cancer treatment. It is a barrier method that is inserted into the uterus.

nodes.label: Metastasis
nodes.description: The spread of cancer from its original site to other parts of the body, specifically mentioned in the context of cancer found in a regional lymph node, referred to as a lymph node metastasis. Metastasis refers to the spread of cancer cells from the original tumor to other parts of the body, such as lymph nodes, bones, or internal organs. Prostate cancer may metastasize to these locations, and a biopsy of a metastasis may be performed to diagnose and evaluate the spread of the disease.

nodes.label: CSCC
nodes.description: Squamous cell carcinoma, a type of skin cancer that can form in scars or chronic wounds, and is the second most common type of skin cancer. It is highly treatable and can often be cured, but can be difficult to treat if it starts in damaged, inflamed, or scarred skin. Risk factors include sunburns, excessive sun exposure, actinic keratoses, weakened immune system, and certain genetic syndromes. CSCC can form in old wounds, burns, or scars, which is known as Marjolin’s ulcer and may be harder to treat. Diagnosis involves a complete head-to-toe skin exam, lymph node exam, and possibly a skin biopsy. Treatment options include Mohs surgery, radiation therapy, and systemic therapy with PD-1 inhibitors. CSCC is also known as squamous cell skin cancer and can be local or regional, affecting the skin and potentially spreading to nearby lymph nodes.

nodes.label: Blood Stem Cells
nodes.description: Early blood-forming cells found in bone marrow. All types of blood cells are created from these stem cells through a process called differentiation. Early blood-forming cells found in bone marrow that give rise to all types of blood cells, including red blood cells, white blood cells, and platelets. They undergo differentiation into mature cells as needed. Early blood-forming cells that multiply to maintain a supply throughout our lifetime. Some of these stem cells gradually develop into blood cells through a process called differentiation.

nodes.label: Folders
nodes.description: Organizational containers for holding documents, used in a medical binder to categorize insurance forms, medical records, and test results. Organizational tools used to categorize and store insurance forms, test types, treatments, and procedures. Folders used in a medical binder to organize items by type, such as insurance forms, test types, treatments, and procedures, with items organized by date for easy reference.

nodes.label: Heart disease
nodes.description: A broad term for conditions that affect the heart and blood vessels, such as coronary artery disease, heart attack, or stroke. It is a medical condition that can run in families and is important for healthcare providers to assess an individual's risk of developing it based on their family history. Heart disease is an example of a health issue to be asked about when gathering family history information.

nodes.label: Actinic keratoses
nodes.description: A type of pre-cancerous lesion that can be treated with photodynamic therapy, cryotherapy, and topical therapy.

nodes.label: Online Patient Portals
nodes.description: Digital platforms accessible through the internet, used for viewing test results and other medical records, often provided by healthcare providers. These portals allow patients to access their medical test results and other health information online, and are recommended for accessing and downloading medical records to add to the medical binder. They often provide features for patient convenience, such as the ability to download or print results.

nodes.label: Risk factors
nodes.description: Risk factors are characteristics or conditions that increase the likelihood of developing liver cancer, particularly in individuals with cirrhosis or chronic hepatitis B. These include hepatitis B virus or infection, hepatitis C virus or infection, alcohol use, non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD), genetic hemochromatosis, stage 4 primary biliary cholangitis, alpha-1-antitrypsin deficiency, other causes of cirrhosis, high alcohol use, and certain demographic characteristics such as being an Asian male assigned sex at birth 40 years of age or over, an Asian female assigned sex at birth 50 years of age or over, or an African/North American Black person with hepatitis B.

nodes.label: Vaping
nodes.description: The illegal act of using electronic cigarettes or similar devices, which can increase the risk of developing certain types of cancer and negatively affect cancer treatment outcomes and wound healing. A harmful behavior involving the inhalation of vapor from electronic cigarettes or similar devices, associated with increased risk of developing various types of cancer, including head and neck, lung, and other cancers. Like smoking, it can limit the effectiveness of cancer treatment and prevent wound healing, as well as increase the risk of side effects during and after surgery. The act of inhaling and exhaling the vapor produced by electronic cigarettes or similar devices, a behavior that shares health risks and impacts with smoking. It increases the risk of developing various cancers and negatively affects cancer treatment and wound healing. The act of inhaling and exhaling the vapor produced by electronic cigarettes or similar devices, identified as a harmful behavior that can negatively impact health, particularly in the context of cancer treatment and surgery.

nodes.label: CLL
nodes.description: Abbreviation for chronic lymphocytic leukemia, a type of blood cancer that grows slowly and may not require treatment for years. It is characterized by the presence of cancerous lymphocytes in the blood, which are a type of white blood cell. Chronic lymphocytic leukemia, a type of cancer where abnormal B cells grow out of control, crowding out healthy B cells and preventing them from performing their duties effectively. A type of blood cancer characterized by an overproduction of abnormal white blood cells, specifically B cells, and is associated with changes or mutations in the bone marrow. A type of blood cancer characterized by an overproduction of monoclonal B lymphocytes, requiring a diagnosis of at least 5,000 or more of the same white blood cells per microliter in the blood. A diagnosis may involve a biopsy of lymph nodes or bone marrow, which can also confirm small lymphocytic lymphoma (SLL). A type of blood cancer, the treatment of which is planned based on the pathology report and other tests. Chronic lymphocytic leukemia, a type of cancer for which biomarkers are used to select treatment, discussed in Chapter 4 of the text.

nodes.label: Biopsy
nodes.description: A medical procedure involving the removal and examination of a small sample of tissue from the body for laboratory analysis, used to diagnose various medical conditions, including cancer, and to determine the presence or absence of cancer cells. It may involve the removal of a sample of tissue, fluid, or skin, and is often used in conjunction with other tests and procedures to confirm a diagnosis or guide treatment decisions.

nodes.label: CT scan
nodes.description: A type of scan often combined with a PET scan (PET/CT) to determine where the cancer cells are located. A medical imaging technique that uses x-rays and computer technology to take pictures of the inside of the body from different angles, combining them into one detailed image. Intravenous (IV) contrast is often used in CT scans. A type of medical imaging test, often used for diagnostic purposes, that involves scanning the body and can be done in the radiology department using a big machine that looks like a tunnel. An imaging technique used in contrast to MRI, involving radiation and used to learn the extent of anal cancer in the pelvis. A medical imaging technique used to obtain pictures of the cancer sites before treatment begins.

nodes.label: Premature menopause
nodes.description: A condition where menopause occurs before the natural age of onset, often caused by surgical removal of both ovaries, leading to a sudden drop in estrogen levels and associated symptoms.

nodes.label: Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia (CLL)
nodes.description: A type of cancer that affects blood and immune cells, described in detail in the patient guide book. It includes information on testing, treatment, monitoring, and supportive care. A type of cancer affecting blood and immune cells, diagnosed through blood tests and biopsies. It involves the presence of monoclonal B lymphocytes in the blood. CLL often has a common pattern of surface proteins on its cells, such as CD20, CD200, and LEF1. A type of cancer affecting the blood and bone marrow, characterized by an overproduction of white blood cells. Symptoms include fever, night sweats, unexplained weight loss, and potential swelling in lymph nodes, the spleen, and the liver. There is an increased risk of developing CLL if there is a family history, and it can be diagnosed through physical examination and blood tests, which may reveal high white blood cell counts. A type of cancer affecting the blood and bone marrow, characterized by an overproduction of white blood cells. The speaker had a consultation with a specialist for this condition and is considering fertility preservation options due to potential treatment impacts. A type of blood cancer affecting the lymphatic system, characterized by the presence of CLL cells in the blood and bone marrow. It is mentioned in the context of biomarkers and treatment options.

nodes.label: Imaging
nodes.description: A medical procedure used to decide whether a biopsy is needed, often paired with a digital rectal exam and PSA test. A diagnostic tool used to determine the extent of the cancer before treatment. A general term for medical procedures used to create visual representations of the body's internal structures. Imaging tests may be used to diagnose, stage, or monitor bladder cancer. A diagnostic procedure used for surveillance of anal cancers in complete remission after treatment, recommended every year for 3 years.

nodes.label: Treatment planning
nodes.description: A process that involves evaluating various factors such as diagnostic test results, cancer stage, individual's overall health, and potential benefits and risks of different treatment options to develop a personalized treatment plan for cancer, starting with testing and organizing medical documents and contact information for the care team.

nodes.label: Adrenal tumors
nodes.description: Adrenal tumors are tumors that can be found in the adrenal glands in one or both adrenal glands. Most tumors found on the adrenal glands are benign (not cancer), but some can be malignant, leading to adrenal cancer.

nodes.label: Brain Tumors
nodes.description: A general term for abnormal growths in the brain, including gliomas, that can disrupt important brain functions. They often start with an abnormality in certain cells leading to uncontrolled cell growth, which is not typically a hereditary mutation. A general term for abnormal growths in the brain, which can cause various symptoms including seizures, fatigue, nausea, and others. A general term for tumors that affect the brain, characterized by an insidious symptom burden that can include personality changes, language and memory impairment, physical impairment, and poor prognosis.

nodes.label: T-ALL
nodes.description: A type of cancer mentioned in the text, characterized by the growth of T-cell lymphoblasts in the thymus rather than the bone marrow. A type of acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) that originates in T-cell lymphocytes, less common than B-ALL, and involves lymphoblasts. T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia, a type of ALL that starts in T-cell lymphocytes. It can cause an enlarged thymus, leading to breathing problems. In some cases, T-cell lymphoblasts grow mostly in the thymus instead of the bone marrow, leading to T-cell lymphoblastic lymphoma (T-LL or T-LBL).

nodes.label: Vyxeos
nodes.description: A dual-drug liposome of cytarabine and daunorubicin, an antimetabolite and an anthracycline, used in chemotherapy to treat AML.

nodes.label: Simulation
nodes.description: A planning session needed before external beam radiation therapy (EBRT) begins, involving being placed in the treatment position. A planning session needed before EBRT begins, involving the patient lying on their back, staying still, and getting fitted for a prop to help stay still during radiation sessions. Pictures of the cancer site(s) are obtained with a CT scan, and using CT images and sophisticated computer software, a treatment plan is made specifying the radiation dose(s) and the number of sessions needed. A planning session before radiation treatment where the patient is placed in the treatment position and a CT scan or other type of scan is done to create a radiation plan tailored to the patient's body and cancer. A planning session before treatment begins where pictures of the cancer sites are obtained with a CT scan, and the radiation team plans the best radiation dose and number of treatments using sophisticated computer software. A procedure where the patient lies on their back with their knees out to the side, often referred to as 'frog-legged', to obtain pictures of the cancer sites with a CT scan before treatment begins.

nodes.label: BRCA mutations
nodes.description: BRCA mutations, specifically BRCA1 and BRCA2, are important biomarkers used to plan ovarian cancer treatment. They are often tested in tumor tissue, and their presence can impact treatment decisions. Genetic testing of the blood for inherited BRCA mutations is different from testing the tumor for BRCA mutations. Mutations in the BRCA genes, particularly BRCA1 and BRCA2, that can increase the risk of breast, ovarian, prostate, colorectal, pancreatic, and melanoma skin cancers, and may affect the efficacy of certain treatments.

nodes.label: Light
nodes.description: A form of energy used in photodynamic therapy (PDT) to activate a light-sensitive drug. The light can be either red or blue light in the doctor’s office or shaded outdoor light. A small light source integrated into the scope, used to illuminate the area being examined.

nodes.label: Fertility Preservation
nodes.description: A set of guidelines or practices aimed at preserving fertility in adolescents and young adults, detailed on the NCCN website and in the NCCN Patient Guides for Cancer app. A service or process for maintaining fertility, particularly relevant for adolescents and young adults, with more information available at NCCN.org/patientguidelines and on the NCCN Patient Guides for Cancer app. A set of options for preserving fertility before starting treatment, discussed with a fertility counselor. A set of options for preserving the ability to have children after cancer treatment. The text mentions sperm banking, egg freezing, and ovarian tissue banking as examples of fertility preservation methods.

nodes.label: Follicular lymphoma (FL)
nodes.description: A common type of non-Hodgkin lymphoma (NHL) that is a slow-dividing, slow-growing B-cell lymphoma typically forming tumors in lymph nodes but can also form in other parts of the body such as the bone marrow, called extranodal disease. It involves the grouping together of excess amounts of abnormal B lymphocytes to form clusters (follicles) in the lymph nodes. A slow-growing (indolent) type of lymphoma that typically forms tumors in the lymph nodes. It involves the formation of clusters (follicles) of abnormal B lymphocytes in the germinal centers of lymph nodes. Not everyone with FL needs treatment immediately.

nodes.label: Dual-drug liposome of cytarabine and daunorubicin (CPX-351 or Vyxeos)
nodes.description: Dual-drug liposome of cytarabine and daunorubicin (CPX-351 or Vyxeos) is a combination drug that includes an antimetabolite and an anthracycline used in the treatment of certain medical conditions. CPX-351 or Vyxeos is a dual-drug liposome containing cytarabine and daunorubicin. It is used in treatment regimens for leukemia and is an example of a combination therapy that includes an anthracycline and an antimetabolite.

nodes.label: Fertility
nodes.description: The ability to conceive and carry a pregnancy to term, which can be affected by certain types of cancer treatment. A concept related to the ability to have children, which may require preservation measures before starting treatment. An important consideration for individuals who may want to have children in the future or are unsure about their future fertility. A biological capacity related to the ability to conceive and carry a pregnancy to term, which can be affected by cancer treatment.

nodes.label: Personal Treatment Decisions
nodes.description: Treatment decisions that are based on individual preferences, values, and circumstances, recognizing that what is important to one person may not be to another.

nodes.label: Urologist
nodes.description: A doctor who specializes in treating diseases of the urinary system and the male reproductive organs, often performing prostate biopsies. A medical doctor specializing in treating diseases of the urinary system and the male reproductive organs. They perform the biopsy procedure, inserting a lubricated probe into the rectum to provide a visual image of the prostate and then inserting a hollow needle into the prostate gland using the video display to guide it. The needle is inserted either through the rectum or through the perineum. They typically take 12 or more core samples from different parts of the prostate and remove the needle, pulling out a small sample of prostate tissue called a core. After the biopsy, they send the samples to a lab for testing. A doctor who specializes in diseases of the urinary system and the male reproductive organs. They perform prostate biopsies and insert a lubricated probe into the rectum to provide a visual image of the prostate. A medical professional who specializes in the diagnosis and treatment of diseases of the urinary tract and the male genital organs. Urologists perform procedures like cystoscopy and collect urine samples for testing. A medical professional who performs surgical procedures for bladder cancer, such as TURBT, by guiding an instrument with a small cutting device through the urethra and into the bladder to remove the tumor. A medical professional who specializes in the diagnosis and treatment of diseases related to the urinary tract and the male reproductive system. A medical professional who specializes in the diagnosis and treatment of disorders of the urinary system and the male reproductive system. Patients are advised to discuss the risks, benefits, and side effects of a radical cystectomy with their urologist and treatment team.

nodes.label: Breast MRI
nodes.description: An imaging test used in the diagnostic process for breast health, potentially supplemented by a diagnostic mammogram and ultrasound as needed. A medical imaging technique that uses radio waves and powerful magnets to take pictures of the inside of the body, often used in addition to a mammogram to look at specific areas of the breast. A type of MRI scan used to image the breast, often used in addition to a mammogram. Contrast should be used. A specific type of MRI used for detecting breast cancer, often used in addition to a mammogram. It involves positioning the patient face down in the machine with arms above the head and the use of contrast material.

nodes.label: Imaging Tests
nodes.description: A type of test to be organized and stored in folders, used to take pictures of the inside of the body. Diagnostic procedures that take pictures of the inside of the body to identify sites with leukemia outside the bone marrow, such as lymph nodes, liver, spleen, and skin. They can also reveal areas of infection or bleeding that may impact care. Tests that take pictures of the inside of the body to look for sites with leukemia outside the bone marrow, such as lymph nodes, liver, spleen, skin, and the lining of the brain and spinal cord. Can also show areas of infection or bleeding that may impact care. Diagnostic tests that produce visual images of the body's internal structures, used to identify cancer, assess its size, location, and spread. A component of the clinical stage rating, used to visualize and assess the cancer and its spread. Medical tests that are interpreted by a radiologist, including x-rays, computed tomography (CT), positron emission tomography (PET), magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), and ultrasound.

nodes.label: Stent
nodes.description: A medical device, specifically a mesh metal tube, that can be placed during surgery to keep the colon open, allowing gas and stool to pass. It is an alternative to a colostomy in addressing bowel blockage caused by a large tumor.

nodes.label: Nasopharynx
nodes.description: One of the three parts of the pharynx, located behind the nose, opens into the larynx and esophagus. The upper part of the throat near the nasal cavity where squamous cell carcinoma can occur. A part of the throat and found inside the neck, connecting the back of the nose (nasal cavity) to the back of the mouth (pharynx). It is a hollow, muscular tube that starts behind the nose and opens into the voice box (larynx) and esophagus. The upper part of the throat near the nasal cavity, one of the three parts of the pharynx, is the area where nasopharyngeal cancer most often occurs.

nodes.label: Pharynx
nodes.description: A part of the body located in the back of the mouth and in the neck, involved in head and neck cancers and located behind the mouth and nose. The pharynx is a part of the throat that starts behind the nose and opens into the larynx and esophagus. It has three parts: nasopharynx, oropharynx, and hypopharynx. Cancer can be found in any part of the pharynx. A part of the throat located behind the mouth and nose, which can be examined using a thin, tubeshaped tool called a scope. A part of the throat found inside the neck, where the nasopharynx connects to the back of the mouth. The part of the throat where the nasopharynx connects, forming part of the throat area.

nodes.label: Squamous cell carcinoma of the head and neck (SCCHN or HNSCC)
nodes.description: The most common type of head and neck cancer, forming in the thin, flat cells of the mucus membranes of the mouth, nose, and throat, including the oropharynx. The most common type of head and neck cancer, forming in the thin, flat cells of the mucus membranes of the mouth (oral), nose (nasal), and throat (pharynx). It is a type of squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) and is the focus of this book. A type of cancer that forms in the thin, flat cells of the mucus membranes of the mouth (oral), nose (nasal), and throat (pharynx), characterized by the presence of squamous cell carcinomas (SCCs). The oropharynx, which includes the back of the roof of the mouth (soft palate), the tonsils, the side and back walls of the throat, and the base of the tongue, is the focus of this book.

nodes.label: Local Excision
nodes.description: A surgical treatment option for some early-stage, low-risk perianal cancers, involving the removal of only the tumor and a small area of surrounding tissue. It is recommended for stages I and IIA perianal cancers with a low or intermediate grade and no invasion of the sphincter muscle.

nodes.label: Lymphocytes
nodes.description: A type of white blood cell that is formed from lymphoid progenitor cells after maturation and plays a crucial role in the immune system by recognizing and responding to pathogens. They are found in blood and lymph tissue and normally grow in response to infection or inflammation. There are three main types: B lymphocytes, T lymphocytes, and natural killer (NK) cells. In acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL), excess lymphoblasts mature into lymphocytes, contributing to the disease. When affected by a genetic abnormality, lymphocytes can lead to the development of primary CNS lymphoma, an abnormal overgrowth that leads to this disease.

nodes.label: National Comprehensive Cancer Network®
nodes.description: An alliance of leading cancer centers across the United States that works together to improve cancer care and develops evidence-based cancer care recommendations used by healthcare providers worldwide. These recommendations are frequently updated and are known as the NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology (NCCN Guidelines®). A leading alliance of cancer centers that collaboratively works to improve cancer care through the development of evidence-based cancer care recommendations. The NCCN develops the NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology (NCCN Guidelines®) which are used by healthcare providers worldwide. These guidelines are frequently updated and include the NCCN Guidelines for Patients, which are designed for people with cancer and caregivers and are based on the NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology (NCCN Guidelines®) for various types of Hodgkin Lymphoma. The NCCN is an independent organization that adapts, updates, and hosts the NCCN Guidelines for Patients, and it is supported by funding from the NCCN Foundation® and corporate supporters like Pfizer Inc. A copyright holder mentioned in the text, associated with the information about AML. The copyright is held by the National Comprehensive Cancer Network® and the website is www.nccn.org. A organization that owns the copyright for the book. It is abbreviated as NCCN and its website is www.nccn.org.

nodes.label: General Health Tests
nodes.description: A range of medical tests and assessments conducted to evaluate overall health, which can include blood tests, imaging results, and medical history. A set of health tests described but not specified in detail. A group of possible tests for AML, used to assess a patient's overall health, often conducted in conjunction with other specific health tests like medical history and physical exam. A set of medical tests described in a guide for treatment planning, including a medical history, tobacco and alcohol use history, and a physical exam, which may include a complete head and neck exam, a mirror exam if needed, screening for depression, a nasopharyngeal fiberoptic exam, and biopsies of tumor or neck, MRI with contrast of collarbone to skull base, and CT of skull base and neck.

nodes.label: Immunotherapy
nodes.description: A type of systemic therapy that uses the body's immune system to fight cancer cells, often involving immune checkpoint inhibitors. It can be used alone or in combination with other therapies like chemotherapy, targeted therapy, or hormone therapy. Immunotherapy is a treatment option for various types of cancer, including prostate, breast, anal, and cervical cancer, and may be particularly effective for cancers with specific biomarkers. It can also cause side effects, such as hepatitis B reactivation.

nodes.label: B cells
nodes.description: Also known as B lymphocytes, B cells are a type of white blood cell made in the bone marrow that leave to work in the bloodstream. A type of white blood cell that plays a vital role in the immune system, particularly in producing antibodies and fighting infections. A type of white blood cell found in the lymph system that plays a role in the immune response and is overproduced in individuals with CLL. A type of white blood cell called a lymphocyte that makes antibodies to fight infections and is an important part of the lymphatic system. B cells are associated with Cutaneous B-cell lymphoma (CBCL).

nodes.label: Care team
nodes.description: A group of healthcare professionals and support staff involved in the diagnosis, treatment, and management of a patient's condition. This may include primary care physicians, specialists, nurses, and other medical personnel who work together to provide comprehensive care for the patient. Patients are encouraged to communicate effectively with their care team, especially in emergency situations, and to be prepared to share medical history and current symptoms.

nodes.label: Chemoradiation
nodes.description: A treatment strategy involving the concurrent use of EBRT and chemotherapy, recommended for most locally advanced cervical cancers that have grown beyond the cervix but have not spread to the liver, lungs, or bones. A combined treatment approach for anal canal cancer involving both chemotherapy and radiation therapy during the same time period. It is used for treating stages I – III anal canal cancer.

nodes.label: Lymphatic System
nodes.description: A major part of the body’s immune system, including lymph vessels, lymph nodes, tonsils, thymus, spleen, and bone marrow. It carries lymphatic fluid (lymph) and white blood cells into all the tissues of the body. A major part of the body’s immune system, responsible for transporting lymph and containing lymph nodes, vessels, and tissues. It includes lymphocytes and is involved in the production of antibodies.

nodes.label: Pancreatic Cancer
nodes.description: A type of cancer that affects cell growth in the pancreas. It causes cells to grow and divide uncontrollably, forming tumors that may spread to other parts of the body. A type of cancer that affects the pancreas, with various stages based on the size of the tumor and the extent of its spread. Stage 0 is only in the innermost layer of the duct wall, Stage 1 involves a tumor 4 centimeters or smaller not outside the pancreas, Stage 2 involves a larger tumor or spread to nearby lymph nodes, Stage 3 grows through the pancreas to nearby major arteries or spreads to 4 or more lymph nodes, and Stage 4 spreads far, commonly involving the liver, lungs, or lining of the abdomen. Metastatic cancer, such as Stage 4, has spread far from the pancreas. A type of cancer that can be associated with germline mutations in genes such as BRCA1, BRCA2, ATM, CHEK2, and others. A type of cancer that can be associated with inherited mutations in genes like BRCA1 and BRCA2.

nodes.label: Capecitabine
nodes.description: A chemotherapy drug that is an antimetabolite and is known to reduce the cells that fight infection. A recommended chemotherapy drug for Stage 2 pMMR/MSS Cancers, given for 6 months. It is also a recommended option for Stage 3 Chemotherapy after colectomy for all stage 3 colon cancers. An anti-cancer medicine used in chemotherapy regimens for anal cancer, often administered in combination with other drugs like mitomycin. It is taken by mouth twice daily, Monday through Friday (on radiation days only), for 5 and a half to 6 weeks during the same time period as radiation therapy. A chemotherapy drug taken by mouth twice daily, Monday through Friday (on radiation days only), for 5 and a half to 6 weeks, often used in combination with mitomycin for chemotherapy regimens. A chemotherapy drug used in the treatment of perianal cancer, which can cause a side effect known as hand-foot syndrome. A chemotherapy drug component of a recommended regimen for treating cancer that returns to lymph nodes in the groin, often used in combination with mitomycin.

nodes.label: Treatment
nodes.description: A general term for medical interventions used to manage or cure various types of cancer, including prostate cancer, stomach cancer, esophageal cancer, gliomas, and mediastinal gray zone lymphoma. Treatment for cancer often involves surgery, radiation, chemotherapy, immunotherapy, targeted therapy, and other methods, and the choice of treatment depends on the type and stage of the cancer, as well as individual patient factors. Fertility preservation may be an important consideration for some patients undergoing treatment for cancer.

nodes.label: CML
nodes.description: Chronic Myeloid Leukemia, a type of cancer characterized by an abnormal increase in white blood cells, particularly granulocytes, and sometimes an imbalance in platelet count. Chronic myeloid leukemia, a type of cancer that affects blood stem cells, causing an increased amount of myeloid progenitor cells. It can progress to an advanced form called blast phase CML (BP-CML), which can cause an increased amount of lymphoid or myeloid progenitor cells. The disease is thought to arise from blood stem cells that make an increased amount of myeloid progenitor cells. Chronic Myeloid Leukemia, a type of cancer discussed in the text, particularly in relation to testing, treatment, and care. Chronic myeloid leukemia, a specific type of cancer mentioned in the text. Chronic Myeloid Leukemia, a type of cancer caused by the uncontrolled blood cell growth triggered by the BCR::ABL1 gene. Chronic myeloid leukemia, a type of cancer diagnosed through testing for biomarkers and genetic changes, requiring accurate testing for diagnosis and treatment.

nodes.label: Head and neck cancers
nodes.description: A category of cancers that arise in the head or neck area of the body, including mouth cancer. They are often treated similarly, and mouth cancer is a type of head and neck cancer. This book does not cover cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma of the vermilion lip, which is a type of head and neck cancer but not of the mouth. Cancers that affect the head and neck region, sometimes spreading to neck lymph nodes. A group of cancers that arise in the head or neck area of the body, including the mouth, middle part of the throat near the mouth, space behind the nose, upper part of the throat near the nasal cavity, voice box, or lower part of the throat behind the larynx. A group of cancers that arise in the head or neck area of the body, including the mouth (oral), nose (nasal), and throat (pharynx). Squamous cell carcinoma of the head and neck (SCCHN or HNSCC) is the most common type of these cancers, forming in the thin, flat cells of the mucus membranes. A type of cancer that affects the head and neck area. The text states that these cancers are not inherited from biological parents, but some cancers and other diseases can run in families, so care teams will ask about the patient's family history regarding these conditions. A group of cancers affecting the head and neck region. They are not inherited from biological parents but can run in families, suggesting a potential genetic or environmental component. The care team collects family history information to assess the risk of these cancers. A group of cancers that arise in the head or neck area of the body, including nasopharyngeal cancer, laryngeal cancer, and esophageal cancer.

nodes.label: Endocrine therapy
nodes.description: A type of treatment used to target hormone receptors found on breast cancer cells, often employed in hormone receptor-positive breast cancer to stop cancer growth or kill cancer cells. It includes the use of tamoxifen or an aromatase inhibitor with testosterone-suppressing therapy for those assigned male at birth whose bodies continue to make testosterone, and may involve the use of GnRH agonists to suppress hormone production. It is not the same as hormone replacement therapy used for menopause and is used to slow tumor growth or shrink the tumor for a period of time. It may be used in combination with CDK4/6 inhibitors and premenopausal individuals must also receive ovarian ablation or suppression.

nodes.label: BRCA1
nodes.description: A gene associated with an increased risk of developing ovarian, breast, and some other cancers, including prostate, pancreatic, and skin cancer (melanoma). Germline mutations in this gene are associated with an increased risk of breast and ovarian cancer in particular. BRCA1 is involved in DNA repair and is one of the genes tested for in molecular tumor marker testing to identify specific abnormalities in DNA repair pathways. When mutated, it can increase the risk of different types of cancer and may impact treatment outcomes, particularly with PARP inhibitors.

nodes.label: Surgery
nodes.description: A medical procedure involving the incision, manipulation, and repair of tissues or organs, often used to remove cancerous tumors or affected tissues. It can be a primary treatment for various types of cancer, such as ovarian, prostate, cervical, thyroid, and bladder cancer, and may involve the removal of cancerous tissue, organs, or entire structures. Surgery may not always be an option, and systemic therapy may continue even if surgery is not feasible. The type of surgery and the organs involved can vary depending on the stage and location of the cancer.

nodes.label: Stereotactic Biopsy
nodes.description: A procedure where a thin, hollow needle is inserted into the brain to remove a sliver of the tumor, followed by sending the sample to a lab to be tested for cancer cells. A very precise procedure often used when a brain tumor is in a hard-to-reach or vital area. It aims to remove only enough of the tumor to make a diagnosis. It is done by a neurosurgeon in an operating room using a computerized navigation system connected to MRI or CT imaging.

nodes.label: Risk Groups
nodes.description: A classification system used by care providers to categorize patients into five different risk groups based on the clinical characteristics of their cancer, such as PSA level, biopsy results, and other test results, ranging from very low risk to very high risk.

nodes.label: BRCA2
nodes.description: A gene associated with an increased risk of developing ovarian, breast, and some other cancers, including prostate, pancreatic, and skin cancer (melanoma). Germline mutations in this gene are associated with an increased risk of breast and ovarian cancer in particular. BRCA2 is involved in DNA repair and is one of the genes tested for in molecular tumor marker testing to identify specific abnormalities in DNA repair pathways. Mutations in this gene can lead to hereditary ovarian cancer, often in combination with BRCA1 gene mutations. When mutated, BRCA2 can increase the risk of breast cancer and is one of the mutations required for PARP inhibitors to be considered as a treatment option.

nodes.label: Treatment Options
nodes.description: A list of methods for treating primary central nervous system lymphoma, including corticosteroids, chemotherapy, radiation therapy, targeted therapy, immunotherapy, stem cell rescue, and supportive care. Some treatments may be combined, such as chemotherapy with an immunotherapy drug.

nodes.label: Bone Marrow
nodes.description: A sponge-like tissue found in the center of most bones, responsible for producing blood cells. It contains blood-forming stem cells that develop into various types of blood cells through a process called differentiation. Sponge-like tissue found in the center of most bones, where blood stem cells are located. It contains early blood-forming cells called blood (hematopoietic) stem cells, which differentiate into various types of blood cells. An organ in the human body that creates blood cells. It is described as a sponge-like tissue in the center of most bones and contains early blood-forming cells called blood (hematopoietic) stem cells.

nodes.label: Vitreous
nodes.description: The clear gel that fills the eye and can be involved in primary CNS lymphoma, also known as vitreoretinal lymphoma when it occurs in the eye. A part of the eye that can look unusual and may require a biopsy if visual symptoms are present. It is also the target of a vitrectomy procedure in the context of primary CNS lymphoma.

nodes.label: Bone
nodes.description: A hard, calcified connective tissue that forms the skeleton of the body, providing support and protection for organs and tissues. It serves multiple functions in the body, including creating blood cells, storing essential chemicals, and producing hormones. Bones contain bone marrow in their center, a sponge-like tissue responsible for the production of blood cells. There are two types of bone: compact bone or cortical bone and spongey bone or cancellous bone. Bone marrow comes in two types: red and yellow, with red marrow containing blood stem cells that can become red blood cells, white blood cells, or platelets, and yellow marrow being mostly fat. Bone is also characterized as being light yet strong and having the ability to regrow. Cancers that start in the bone are called primary bone cancers, while cancers that start in another part of the body and spread to the bone are secondary bone malignancies or metastatic cancer. A site for various types of cancer metastasis, including breast, stomach, and cervical cancer, as well as a common site for metastatic cancer to spread in tumor testing alongside lymph nodes, liver, lung, or other affected areas.

nodes.label: Intravesical Chemotherapy
nodes.description: A one-time dose of chemotherapy given to treat cancer and reduce the risk of recurrence, typically instilled within 24 hours of TURBT surgery. It’s meant to destroy any remaining cancer cells and prevent new growth. It may also be an option if BCG is unavailable or ineffective.

nodes.label: Scope
nodes.description: A long, thin tube with a light and a camera used in medical procedures such as colonoscopy and upper endoscopy. It is inserted into the body to examine internal structures. A medical instrument with a small light and camera lens at one end, used to examine the oropharynx and take pictures. It can be fiberoptic, flexible, or a laryngoscope with a thin, long tube. It is inserted into the mouth or nose and sends images to a television or computer monitor.

nodes.label: Treatment options for bladder cancer
nodes.description: A range of medical interventions used to treat bladder cancer, including surgery, intravesical therapy, systemic therapy, radiation therapy, clinical trials, and supportive care.

nodes.label: Endoscopy
nodes.description: A medical procedure used to examine the oropharynx and take pictures, often involving the use of a scope guided into the body through the mouth or nose. It can help determine the size and spread of a tumor and take a tumor sample. Before the procedure, a topical spray is given to numb the throat. Possible types of endoscopy include fiberoptic nasopharyngolaryngoscopy and laryngoscopy with a laryngoscope.

nodes.label: Blood tests
nodes.description: Blood tests are medical procedures that involve analyzing samples of a patient's blood to measure various components such as blood cells, proteins, and chemicals. They can provide information about the presence and severity of certain conditions, including cancer like chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL). Blood tests can detect high levels of alkaline phosphatase (ALP), which may indicate bone tumors, liver disorders, or pregnancy. They can also measure the levels of red blood cells (RBCs), white blood cells (WBCs), and platelets (PLTs) in the blood. Blood tests are used in the diagnosis, monitoring, and treatment planning of various health conditions, including adrenal tumors, esophageal cancer, ovarian cancer, rectal cancer, AML, CML, ALL, pancreatic cancer, and breast cancer. Results from blood tests are used to guide treatment decisions and monitor a patient's response to treatment.

nodes.label: BRCA genes
nodes.description: A pair of genes (BRCA1 and BRCA2) that, when mutated, can increase the risk of developing ovarian, breast, and other hereditary cancers. Genetic testing can determine if an individual has a mutation in these genes. BRCA status is important in guiding maintenance therapy decisions for ovarian cancer patients. A pair of genes associated with hereditary ovarian cancer, mutations in which can significantly increase the risk of developing the disease. Genetic testing for BRCA mutations is recommended for everyone diagnosed with ovarian cancer. Genes that, when mutated, can increase the risk of developing breast cancer. They are written in italics, for example: BRCA. They are part of biomarker testing. A type of gene that, when functioning normally, helps prevent tumor growth, fix damaged cells, and promote normal cell growth. Mutations in BRCA1 or BRCA2 can significantly increase the risk of various types of cancer.

nodes.label: Test results
nodes.description: Test results are documents that contain the results of diagnostic tests, including blood tests, imaging studies, and biopsies. In the context of esophageal cancer, test results are used to evaluate the presence and extent of tumor involvement and to develop a treatment plan. Documents containing the results of diagnostic tests, including imaging studies, biopsies, and biomarker testing, often organized and managed by patients as part of their throat cancer treatment process. A type of medical document that needs to be organized as part of treatment planning for CML. Documents containing the outcomes of medical tests used to diagnose and treat CML, which patients should organize and understand. Test results are documents that contain the outcomes of various diagnostic tests, such as blood tests, imaging studies, and biopsies. They are an important part of a patient's medical records and are organized alongside other test results, insurance forms, and medical reports.

nodes.label: Imaging
nodes.description: A medical procedure that takes pictures of the inside of the body, such as the chest, to assess lung nodules for cancer. Imaging may be reviewed by a thoracic radiologist and may require additional scans if there may be cancer. Diagnostic imaging tests used to visualize the cervix and surrounding structures, such as ultrasounds or MRIs, to assess the patient's general health and identify potential risk factors for cervical cancer. A diagnostic procedure used to determine the extent of cancer, involving the use of x-rays or other imaging techniques to visualize the size and spread of the cancer. A diagnostic technique used to visualize the internal structures of the body. Imaging results are used in conjunction with biopsy results to assign scores in the TNM system. A diagnostic tool mentioned as potentially used to take a closer look at symptoms, discussed in the text after describing symptoms. The process of taking detailed pictures (images) of the insides of the body, which can show the size, location, and other features of cancer. Imaging can reveal where the cancer started and whether the cancer has spread (metastasized).

nodes.label: Quamous Cell Skin Cancer
nodes.description: A type of skin cancer that can spread through the blood and lymph to form tumors in other areas of the body, known as metastasis. It is less likely to metastasize compared to other types of skin cancer, leading to limited research on treating metastatic forms.

nodes.label: FDG PET-CT
nodes.description: A type of PET-CT scan that uses a radiotracer called F-18 fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG), which is made of fluoride and a simple form of sugar called glucose. It is most helpful when other imaging results are unclear and can help find cancer in lymph nodes and distant sites. It can be done at the same time as a CT used for diagnosis.

nodes.label: MSH2
nodes.description: MSH2 is a gene that, when mutated, can increase the risk of different types of cancer, including prostate, breast, ovarian, pancreatic, and skin cancer (melanoma). Germline mutations in this gene are associated with an increased risk of cancer in general. A gene associated with germline mutations that can put an individual at risk for prostate cancer, colorectal and uterine cancers, and skin cancer (melanoma). MSH2 is a gene that, when mutated, can increase the risk of different types of cancer. It is one of the genes typically looked at in hereditary gene testing for prostate cancer. A gene associated with inherited mutations that can increase the risk of developing certain cancers, including prostate cancer, colorectal cancer, uterine cancer, and other cancers.

nodes.label: Liver
nodes.description: A large, glandular organ located in the upper right portion of the abdomen, responsible for various functions including detoxification, protein synthesis, and production of biochemicals necessary for digestion. It is one of the common sites for metastasis in various types of cancer, such as breast, prostate, stomach, and anal cancer, and can be imaged using MRI to look for signs of cancer spread. The liver is also involved in the digestive system and is one of the organs included in the hepatobiliary system.

nodes.label: Immunohistochemistry (IHC)
nodes.description: A special staining process that involves adding a chemical marker to cells and studying them using a microscope. IHC is used to look for the immunophenotype of cells from a biopsy or tissue sample, helping to identify specific cell types or markers. Immunohistochemistry (IHC) is a special staining process that involves adding a chemical marker to cells and studying them under a microscope. It is used to identify the immunophenotype of cells from a biopsy or tissue sample, helping to diagnose AML. A procedure that involves adding a chemical marker to cells, which are then studied using a microscope. It can detect estrogen, progesterone, and HER2 receptors in breast cancer cells. A pathologist will measure the number of cells with estrogen and/or progesterone receptors and the number of receptors inside each cell.

nodes.label: Colectomy
nodes.description: A surgical procedure used to treat non-metastatic colon cancer, often followed by chemotherapy. Colectomy, or colon surgery, is a surgical procedure used to remove parts of the colon for invasive cancer that cannot be removed by polypectomy. A surgical procedure involving the removal of the part of the colon containing cancer. This is needed for cancers not found early enough to be removed by polypectomy. The procedure involves removing the cancerous part of the colon and sewing or stapling together the two healthy ends of the remaining colon. At least 12 lymph nodes near the tumor and any abnormal-looking nodes are removed and tested for cancer. A colectomy can be done in two ways: the open method and the minimally invasive method. The results of the surgery are used to assign the cancer a stage, which helps determine whether chemotherapy is needed after surgery. In some cases, a colostomy may also be performed during a colectomy to attach the remaining upper part of the colon to an opening on the surface of the abdomen. A surgical procedure for removing part or all of the colon, often performed in cases of colon cancer. It can be done as a one-stage procedure to unblock the bowel or with a colostomy, which is typically reversed with another operation. A colectomy may also involve the placement of a mesh metal tube called a stent to keep the colon open. A surgical procedure for removing part or all of the colon, often performed in conjunction with systemic therapy for dMMR/MSI-H cancers. A surgical procedure mentioned in the context of chemotherapy recommendations for stage 1, 2, and 3 colon cancers.

nodes.label: External Beam Radiation Therapy (EBRT)
nodes.description: A type of radiation therapy that uses high-energy waves similar to x-rays to kill cancer cells, typically delivered in small doses called fractions. It is often used in combination with other treatments for various types of cancer, such as cervical, rectal, bladder, and anal cancer. EBRT can involve the use of a large machine aiming radiation at the cancer site and may include procedures like ovarian transposition as part of the treatment plan.

nodes.label: Complete Blood Count (CBC)
nodes.description: A possible test for AML, often used in conjunction with other tests like a differential, CMP, uric acid, LDH, B12, and folic acid to assess a patient's blood cell counts and overall health. A common blood test that measures the levels of red blood cells (RBCs), white blood cells (WBCs), and platelets (PLTs) in the blood. It provides a picture of overall health and can detect abnormalities in blood cell counts, such as high blasts, which may indicate AML. Key measurements include hemoglobin (Hgb), platelets (PLTs), and absolute neutrophil count (ANC). A type of blood test that may be ordered as part of diagnostic testing for cervical cancer recurrence. A blood test used in conjunction with other tests to check for signs of cancer recurrence. A blood test that measures the levels of red blood cells, white blood cells, and platelets in the blood. It helps determine if a person has enough red blood cells to carry oxygen, white blood cells to fight infection, and platelets to control bleeding.

nodes.label: Care team
nodes.description: A group of healthcare professionals involved in the management and treatment of various types of cancer, including head and neck cancer, breast cancer, and bone cancer. They are responsible for making treatment decisions, managing patients' overall health, and providing support and guidance to patients. Patients are encouraged to play an active role in their care by asking questions and making shared decisions with their care team.

nodes.label: Small Cell Carcinoma
nodes.description: A type of lung cancer that is further divided into small cell carcinoma and combined (small and non-small) cell lung carcinoma. It is a category under non-small cell lung cancer and is usually treated like small cell lung cancer when found in lung tumors. A type of lung cancer characterized by small and blue cells when viewed under a microscope. It is less common than NSCLC and is the focus of the book. Smoking is the main cause of SCLC, and exposure to second-hand smoke and cancer-causing chemicals also increases the risk. Symptoms depend on the location of the lung tumor growth or spread. A type of non-urothelial bladder cancer that starts in the small cells of the bladder lining. This type of cancer is less common than urothelial cell carcinoma.

nodes.label: Surgery
nodes.description: A medical procedure performed to remove cancerous tumors or tissue, particularly in the context of ovarian cancer treatment. It is used to determine the extent of cancer in the body and may involve the removal of a sample of the tumor for testing. A gynecologic oncologist, an expert in surgery and chemotherapy for gynecologic cancers, should perform the initial surgery. A medical procedure performed to remove cancerous tissue and nearby lymph nodes, providing important information for pathologic staging and determining treatment options after surgery. A medical procedure involving the removal of all or part of the tumor and nearby lymph nodes, used in throat cancer staging to gain information about the spread of cancer. A medical procedure that may be required to remove the biopsy site or treat any abnormalities found during the biopsy. A medical procedure involving the cutting of the body for various reasons, such as treatment or diagnosis. The text states that smoking and vaping greatly increase the chances of having side effects during and after surgery.

nodes.label: Testing For Stomach Cancer
nodes.description: A process involving various tests for detecting stomach cancer, including general health tests, nutrition assessment, blood tests, imaging tests, endoscopy procedures, H. pylori tests, biopsy, biomarker testing, genetic risk testing, and performance status assessment.

nodes.label: Imaging tests
nodes.description: Imaging tests are non-invasive medical procedures that use various technologies to visualize internal structures and organs in the body. They are used to diagnose and monitor medical conditions, including cancer, and are often performed alongside other tests such as biopsy, genetic risk testing, and performance status assessment. Imaging tests can detect abnormalities and help determine a treatment plan.

nodes.label: Photodynamic Therapy (PDT)
nodes.description: A type of treatment where a light-sensitive drug is applied to the area. When exposed to light (either red or blue light in the doctor’s office, or shaded outdoor light), the drug becomes active and kills cancer cells. It is used to treat superficial treatments and certain types of skin cancer. A superficial treatment where a drug applied to the skin becomes active and kills cancer cells when exposed to light, with common side effects including itching or burning, pain during light exposure, and skin redness.

nodes.label: Treatment Surgery
nodes.description: A medical procedure recommended to treat squamous cell skin cancer that has spread to nearby lymph nodes, involving the excision of the cancerous lesion and nearby lymph nodes.

nodes.label: Complete blood count (CBC)
nodes.description: A common blood test that measures various components of the blood, including white blood cells, red blood cells, and platelets. It can also include a differential, which counts the most common types of white blood cells and checks if their counts are in balance with each other. Used to assess overall health and detect potential issues with the blood or immune system, and is not used alone to diagnose colon cancer.

nodes.label: TNM
nodes.description: A system used to assign a stage to cancer based on the depth and size of the main tumor, the spread to nearby lymph nodes, and the presence of metastasis. An example of a TNM staging might look like T1N0M0 or T1, N0, M0, indicating the tumor's depth and size, the absence of spread to regional lymph nodes, and the absence of metastasis.

nodes.label: Specific type of cancer
nodes.description: The particular type of cancer a patient has, for which copies of blood tests, imaging results, and reports should be obtained. Specific type of cancer refers to the particular form or subtype of cancer that a patient has been diagnosed with. In the context of liver cancer, this could include different types of liver cancer, such as hepatocellular carcinoma or cholangiocarcinoma. Patients are encouraged to obtain copies of their test results and reports related to their specific type of cancer to better understand their condition and engage in their care. The exact type of cancer a patient has, which may include details about its location, stage, and other characteristics. Patients are advised to obtain copies of reports about their specific type of cancer as part of organizing their medical records and papers related to their cancer care.

nodes.label: Bone Marrow
nodes.description: A sponge-like tissue found in the center of most bones, containing blood stem cells that develop into various types of blood cells. It is a crucial site for blood cell production and is involved in the body's immune response. There are two types: red and yellow. Red marrow contains blood stem cells that can become red blood cells, white blood cells, or platelets, while yellow marrow is made mostly of fat. Bone marrow tests are often performed, with samples typically taken from the back of the hip bone (pelvis). It can be affected by cancer and its treatment, leading to a need for stem cell rescue.

nodes.label: Lymph nodes
nodes.description: Small, bean-shaped structures that are part of the immune system and are found throughout the body. They filter lymph fluid and contain immune cells, helping to fight infection and remove harmful substances, including cancer cells. Lymph nodes can become enlarged due to cancer or other diseases, and can be affected by various types of cancer, such as prostate, pancreatic, ovarian, stomach, bladder, head and neck, thyroid, and skin cancers. They can also be removed during surgery for conditions like ovarian cancer, thyroid cancer, or papillary cancers, and are often biopsied to check for cancer cells. In the context of the lymphatic system, lymph nodes are crucial for maintaining overall health and preventing the spread of cancer.

nodes.label: Care Team
nodes.description: A group of healthcare professionals involved in a patient's medical care, including doctors, nurses, and other specialists, who provide guidance, support, and treatment for patients with cancer or related conditions. They are responsible for gathering a patient's health information, monitoring their condition, and managing their care, including discussing treatment options and concerns related to fertility and pregnancy. Patients are encouraged to discuss their care, share their concerns, and ask questions with their care team.

nodes.label: Supportive care
nodes.description: A comprehensive approach to managing symptoms, side effects, and quality of life for patients with acute myeloid leukemia (AML), prostate cancer, or bladder cancer. It includes measures to improve quality of life, such as pain management, emotional support, and other interventions.

nodes.label: Photodynamic Therapy
nodes.description: A superficial treatment where a light-sensitive drug is applied to the area and becomes active when exposed to light, killing cancer cells. A treatment option for actinic keratoses, which are pre-cancerous lesions. It involves the use of light and a photosensitizing agent to destroy abnormal cells.

nodes.label: Regional CSCC
nodes.description: A type of squamous cell carcinoma that has spread to nearby lymph nodes. The goal of testing for regional cancer is to determine how and where the cancer has spread so that the best treatment plan can be determined. A type of squamous cell skin cancer that is discussed in the text, involving surgery to remove the tumor and nearby lymph nodes as the best treatment method. A specific type of CSCC that is in nearby lymph nodes, requiring more frequent monitoring during the first 2 years after treatment. A specific type of CSCC that is in nearby lymph nodes, requiring physical exams with skin checks every 2 to 3 months for 1 year, every 2 to 4 months for the second year, every 4 to 6 months for another 3 years, and then every 6 to 12 months for the rest of your life.

nodes.label: White Blood Cells
nodes.description: A type of blood cell that fights infections. They are also known as leukocytes and include granulocytes, monocytes, and lymphocytes. White blood cells (WBCs or leukocytes) play a crucial role in fighting infections. They include granulocytes, monocytes, and lymphocytes, which are formed from lymphoid progenitor cells. A type of blood cell that plays a crucial role in the immune system, helping to prevent and control infection. They are formed from blood stem cells and include granulocytes, such as neutrophils, which are types of immune cells. A type of blood cell that fights infections. Includes granulocytes, monocytes, and lymphocytes. Also known as leukocytes or WBCs.

nodes.label: Classic FL
nodes.description: A classification of follicular lymphoma based on the International Consensus classification (ICC) system, which includes grades 1 and 2. It is also known as cFL in the 2022 World Health Organization classification (WHO5). A type of follicular lymphoma (FL) that is grade 1, characterized by a chromosome translocation or excess levels of the BCL2 protein in the tumor. It is the most common form of FL described in the text.

nodes.label: Biopsy
nodes.description: A medical procedure involving the removal and examination of a small sample of tissue to confirm the presence of cancer or other abnormalities. Biopsies can be performed using various techniques, such as fine-needle aspiration, core needle biopsy, or surgical excision, and the samples are typically sent to a laboratory for analysis by a pathologist. Biopsies are often used in the diagnosis and treatment of cancer, including bladder cancer, and can help confirm a diagnosis when imaging tests are inconclusive.

nodes.label: Sentinel Lymph Node Biopsy (SLNB or SNB)
nodes.description: A surgical procedure to remove sentinel lymph nodes during surgery such as a mastectomy or lumpectomy to determine if any cancer cells have traveled to the lymph nodes. It involves injecting a radioactive material and other dyes into the area where the breast tumor is located, which helps the surgeon find the sentinel lymph nodes.

nodes.label: Pathologic Stage
nodes.description: A rating determined by examining tissue removed during surgery, often denoted as pN or surgical stage. The staging determined by examining tissue removed during surgery, providing more accurate details about the size of the cancer and lymph node status. It is denoted by the letter 'p' and is used to determine treatment options after surgery. A stage in throat cancer staging based on information gained after surgery to remove all or part of the tumor and nearby lymph nodes, providing a more accurate picture of how far the cancer has spread and used to determine treatment options after surgery. A rating determined by examining tissue removed during surgery, also known as surgical stage. Examples include pN or ypT. The stage determined by examining tissue removed during surgery, often denoted as pN or surgical stage. An example is pN, indicating the status of lymph nodes based on surgical examination.

nodes.label: SCC
nodes.description: Squamous cell carcinoma, the most common type of mouth cancer and the focus of this book. It forms in the thin, flat cells of the mucous membranes of the mouth and is the most common type of mouth cancer. Squamous cell carcinoma, the most common type of mouth cancer, forming in the thin, flat cells of the mucous membranes of the mouth. Squamous cell carcinoma, a type of cancer that affects the mucus membranes of the nasopharynx. It is the focus of the book chapter discussed in the text.

nodes.label: Basal Cells
nodes.description: A type of cell found in the epidermis, which can become abnormal and grow out of control, leading to basal cell skin cancer. They are flat cells located in the upper part of the epidermis. A type of cell found in the lower part of the epidermis, which constantly divide to form new cells that replace the squamous cells on the skin’s surface. Cells found in the lower part of the epidermis, called the basal cell layer. They constantly divide to form new cells to replace the squamous cells that wear off the skin's surface.

nodes.label: Transformation Zone
nodes.description: The area where the ectocervix and endocervix meet, which is removed during cone biopsy. Most cervical cancers start in this area. The area where the ectocervix and endocervix meet, often the site of cervical cancers and the target of cone biopsies.

nodes.label: Lymphoma
nodes.description: A type of cancer that originates in the lymphatic system, specifically affecting lymphocytes, which are white blood cells that fight infections. It can be either Hodgkin or non-Hodgkin, and may be slow-growing (indolent) or aggressive. Lymphoma can involve the formation of tumor clusters in the lymph nodes or other parts of the body, and can be targeted by high-dose chemotherapy in a stem cell rescue procedure. The exact cause of lymphoma is not known, but genetic abnormalities are involved. Primary CNS lymphoma is a specific type of lymphoma that most often affects the brain.

nodes.label: TNM system
nodes.description: A system created by cancer experts to describe tumors based on the results of imaging scans, biopsies, and blood tests, categorizing tumors into different stages based on the presence and extent of cancer in the tumor, nodes, and metastases. A staging system used by the American Joint Committee on Cancer to describe the extent of colon cancer in the body, based on tumor size, lymph node involvement, and metastasis. A staging system used to describe the growth and spread of most bone cancers. It uses the letters T, N, and M to describe different areas of cancer growth based on imaging and biopsy results. The higher the number assigned to each letter, the larger the tumor or the more the cancer has spread to lymph nodes or other organs. These scores are combined to assign the cancer a stage. An example TNM score might look like this: T1N0M0 or T1, N0, M, representing a stage 1 cancer.

nodes.label: Doctor
nodes.description: A medical professional who diagnoses, treats, and provides expert advice and guidance on test results, treatment plans, and fertility-related risks associated with cancer treatment. They may perform various examinations, take biopsies, and discuss imaging test results with patients. Doctors with experience in diagnosing and treating specific types of cancer, such as bone cancer, are highly sought after. They also play a crucial role in advising patients on fertility preservation, birth control options, and planning a pregnancy after cancer treatment. In some cases, they may recommend additional tests, such as an HIV test, and consult with other medical professionals, like radiologists, to ensure comprehensive patient care.

nodes.label: PALB2
nodes.description: PALB2 is a gene that, when mutated, can increase the risk of different types of cancer, including prostate, breast, ovarian, pancreatic, and skin cancer (melanoma). Germline mutations in this gene are associated with an increased risk of breast and pancreatic cancer in particular. A gene associated with germline mutations that can put an individual at risk for prostate cancer, breast cancer, ovarian cancer, pancreatic cancer, and skin cancer (melanoma). PALB2 is a gene that, when mutated, can increase the risk of different types of cancer. It is one of the genes typically looked at in hereditary gene testing for prostate cancer. A gene associated with inherited mutations that can increase the risk of developing certain cancers, including prostate cancer. A gene involved in DNA repair, associated with an increased risk of developing certain types of cancer. It is one of the genes tested for in molecular tumor marker testing to identify specific abnormalities in DNA repair pathways.

nodes.label: Bone cancer
nodes.description: A group of cancers that start in the bone or cartilage, called primary bone cancer, or spread to the bone from another part of the body, known as secondary bone malignancies or metastatic cancer. Bone cancers that start in another part of the body and travel to the bones behave very differently from primary bone cancers. Bone cancer is a type of cancer that affects the bones, with Chapter 2 of the book providing an overview of tests for it, potential impacts on fertility, and the role of biomarker and tumor mutation testing in diagnosis. A rare type of cancer that affects the bones. It requires specialized expertise for diagnosis and treatment, necessitating the need to find healthcare providers with experience in this area. Testing is crucial for accurate diagnosis and treatment planning. Bone cancer is a type of cancer that affects the bones. Some types of treatment for bone cancer can affect fertility, so patients should consider fertility preservation options before starting treatment. A type of cancer that affects the bone, diagnosed using a core needle or surgical biopsy. The placement of the biopsy is critical and should be performed by an experienced surgeon at the center where treatment will be received. A sample from the biopsy might be tested for biomarkers or proteins, and genetic testing may be recommended to learn more about the cancer. Treatment decisions are based on the type of bone cancer, prognosis, and available treatment options.

nodes.label: Colostomy
nodes.description: A surgical procedure where a part of the colon is connected to the outside of the abdomen, creating an opening (a stoma) for stool to exit the body, typically used temporarily or permanently to allow the rectum to heal. A surgical procedure that connects the end of the colon to the outside of the abdomen, creating an opening called a stoma for stool to exit the body. A permanent colostomy is needed after APR to manage stool elimination. A surgical procedure involving the creation of a permanent colostomy for stool to leave the body, often performed as part of APR surgery for anal cancer that does not respond to initial treatment or returns after treatment.

nodes.label: Blood Tests
nodes.description: A type of diagnostic test that involves the analysis of blood samples to check for signs of disease, assess organ function, and monitor treatment plans. Blood tests may be used to detect specific biomarkers, stage cancer, confirm diagnoses, and evaluate general health. They can also be used to check for signs of cancer recurrence, such as the CA-125 level, and to monitor thyroid hormone levels during replacement therapy.

nodes.label: Multidisciplinary Team
nodes.description: A group of doctors, specialists, and allied health providers who work together to help a patient with primary CNS lymphoma, guiding treatment decisions and discussing individual treatment plans.

nodes.label: Squamous Cell Carcinoma
nodes.description: A type of cancer that forms in squamous cells, found in the tissues that form the surface of the skin and in other areas of the body. It is the most common type of anal cancer and can also occur in the bladder lining, cervical cancer, and lung cancer. It is not a type of urothelial cell carcinoma and is one of the categories under non-small cell lung cancer.

nodes.label: Intravesical BCG Therapy
nodes.description: A treatment involving a liquid medicine, BCG, placed directly into the bladder to destroy any cancer cells left behind by TURBT and prevent new cancer cells from forming. It’s given once a week for 6 weeks, followed by maintenance therapy involving three treatments at 3 months, 6 months, and then every 6 months for up to 3 years, depending on the risk of recurrence. Possible side effects include fever, chills, the urge to urinate, pain or difficulty when urinating, and blood or particles in urine.

nodes.label: Blood (Hematopoietic) Stem Cells
nodes.description: Early blood-forming cells found in bone marrow that give rise to all types of blood cells, including red blood cells, white blood cells, and platelets. They are the progenitors of all blood cells. Early blood-forming cells present in bone marrow that multiply to maintain a supply throughout our lifetime. They gradually develop into blood cells through a process called differentiation, eventually becoming red blood cells, white blood cells, or platelets. Early blood-forming cells found in bone marrow that have the ability to develop into different types of blood cells. They are the precursors to red blood cells, white blood cells, and platelets.

nodes.label: Imaging studies
nodes.description: Diagnostic procedures that use imaging technologies to visualize internal structures and organs, such as the lymph nodes, spleen, and other parts of the body. They are used to detect tumors, swelling, or other abnormalities associated with follicular lymphoma (FL). A type of diagnostic test used in AML treatment to evaluate the condition of the patient. Results from blood tests, along with bone marrow aspirate and biopsy, and imaging studies, are used to guide treatment plans. Diagnostic imaging procedures used to identify and locate tumors or other abnormalities associated with ALL. Results from these studies, along with blood and bone marrow tests, are used to determine a patient's treatment plan. A type of test used in the diagnosis of breast cancer, where images of the breast are taken to detect abnormalities or confirm a diagnosis. A test used in treatment planning, involving the use of medical imaging techniques to visualize the internal structures of the body and detect abnormalities. A type of test that uses imaging techniques to visualize internal structures and detect abnormalities. It is part of the testing process for NPC.

nodes.label: Squamous Cells
nodes.description: A type of cell found in the epidermis, specifically in the upper part of the layer. They are flat cells that can form skin cancer when they become abnormal and grow out of control. A type of cell found in the upper part of the epidermis, which are flat cells. Thin, flat cells found in the epidermis that resemble fish scales. They form the surface of the skin and can become scaly patches, eventually leading to skin cancer. Cells that are formed in the epidermis when it gets flatter. They are a type of cell found in the top layer of skin.

nodes.label: Treatment
nodes.description: A general term for medical interventions or therapies used to manage, treat, or cure a disease, particularly cancer, which can impact fertility and require specific considerations. It can involve various methods such as chemotherapy, surgery, radiation therapy, or clinical trials, and is tailored to the individual patient's needs and condition. Treatment can also refer to the process of managing or curing a disease, such as anal cancer, where the goals and methods are discussed, and may include a series of radiation sessions with specific side effects.

nodes.label: CT
nodes.description: A type of medical imaging test that uses contrast, with different types of contrast compared to MRI. A type of imaging test used for diagnosis, which can be done simultaneously with FDG-PET to detect cancer. It is often used in conjunction with ultrasound for guiding biopsies. A medical imaging technique that can be used with PET to form a PET-CT scan, or used for diagnosis at the same time as FDG PET-CT. Computed Tomography, a type of imaging connected to a computerized navigation system for targeting and removing a brain tumor sample with precision. A type of imaging test, specifically a computed tomography scan, for which the contrast material used may differ from that used in magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). A medical imaging technique used in conjunction with a computerized navigation system for tumor removal during a resection procedure. A type of imaging scan commonly used to see how far bladder cancer has spread, often used in conjunction with MRI.

nodes.label: CDK4/6 inhibitors
nodes.description: A class of inhibitors that target the cyclin-dependent kinase (CDK) protein, which helps cells grow and divide. They are used in hormone receptor-positive, HER2- cancer in combination with endocrine therapy. Premenopausal individuals must also receive ovarian ablation or suppression. Examples include abemaciclib (Verzenio), palbociclib (Ibrance), and ribociclib (Kisqali).

nodes.label: PET/CT Scan
nodes.description: A combined imaging technique that involves the use of both PET and CT scans to generate detailed images of the body's internal structures, providing both functional and anatomical information. A type of imaging scan that combines PET and CT scans to show a cross-section of a patient’s pelvis, identifying cancer in the prostate and cancer that has spread to a lymph node in the pelvis. Green represents prostate cancer, while intense red indicates cancer spread to a lymph node.
